ttp-attack-mapping-reliability.rationale: Unchanged from cycle 4; re-checked live rather than assumed. Primary candidate (status: supported) rests on 2 independent sources: src-0002 (CTIBench CTI-ATE F1=0.6388 for GPT-4-turbo, vs ~71-72% on knowledge-recall CTI-MCQ/CTI-RCM) and src-0005 (CyberSOCEval, CrowdStrike/Meta-affiliated 2025-era; test-time-scaling 'reasoning' gains do not transfer to cybersecurity reasoning, 'far from saturating'). Cycle 6's G2 retrospection re-fetched https://arxiv.org/html/2406.07599 and re-confirmed the 0.6388 / 71% / 72% / 86%-plausible-vs-52%-correct figures, so the evidence base is freshly verified. Considered and rejected a rise to 4: src-0006 (added cycle 6) does NOT supply a third source here -- its own limitations note it does not test ATT&CK-technique mapping in the CTI-ATE form, so it cannot address open_questions[0] (does the 0.64 ceiling generalize to 2025-era models). open_questions[1] (human-analyst baseline F1) and [2] (ATT&CK-specific fine-tuning) remain wholly unaddressed, and no counterargument has been explicitly engaged, which is what level 4 requires. No open contradiction, so no g3 demotion.

ioc-extraction-reliability.rationale: Unchanged from cycle 4. Sole candidate's evidence remains src-0003 alone (LANCE 97.6% F1 vs PRISM; legacy tools 76%/72%/86%). Single-source support = 2 per rubric, notwithstanding the candidate's own self-assigned 'supported' status label, which was set at collection time and has never been externally corroborated. Cycle 5's G2 retrospection re-fetched the src-0003 URL and re-confirmed the numbers -- that raises confidence in the source but adds no second source, so it cannot raise the score. Cycle 6 ran a targeted web search for an independent LANCE/PRISM replication or critique and found none published, so open_questions[0] (the authors-share-a-benchmark conflict-of-interest risk, flagged in src-0003's own limitations) is actively unresolved rather than merely unexamined. src-0006 does not test IoC extraction and so does not corroborate here. No open contradiction, so no g3 demotion.

consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode.rationale: Unchanged from cycle 4. Both candidate_resolutions cite evidence=["src-0001"] only; the cycle-3 candidate sharpens the cycle-2 one using the SAME source, so two candidates do not equal two sources. Re-verified this cycle as the G2 retrospection target (see logs/cycle-007.md): re-fetched https://arxiv.org/html/2503.23175v1 and independently re-confirmed the 3 model identities (gpt4o, gemini-1.5-pro-latest, mistral-large-2), the 350-report evaluation set, the 10-re-prompt bootstrapped-CI consistency method with max CI width 0.02 (extraction) vs 0.06 (generation), and all ten Table-6 gpt4o ECE/Brier values including the CVE-generation ECE 0.15->0.91 and attack-vector ECE 0.47->0.87 fine-tuning degradations. All figures held; confidence in src-0001 is now high, but confidence in a single source is still single-source support. Considered whether src-0006 corroborates: rejected -- src-0006 measures cross-task performance variation and uses a 'counterfactual consistency check' as an internal validation device, but does not measure output consistency across repeated/paraphrased queries nor report any confidence-calibration metric (ECE/Brier), which are precisely the two properties this issue is about. open_questions[0-3] (whether the calibration pattern is gpt4o-specific, whether it replicates on src-0002/src-0005's disjoint model lists, whether the framing extends to other CTI sub-tasks, and whether fine-tuning degradation is a dataset-size artifact) all remain unaddressed. No open contradiction, so no g3 demotion.

attribution-confident-wrong-gap.rationale: Unchanged from cycle 4. Evidence remains 2 genuinely independent sources: src-0002 (CTIBench CTI-TAA over 50 real reports; GPT-4-turbo 86% plausible vs 52% correct, Gemini-1.5 74% vs 38%; re-confirmed by cycle 6's live re-fetch) and src-0004 (Heise reporting on ENISA's 2025 Threat Landscape reports; re-confirmed by cycle 4's live re-fetch). Academic benchmark plus investigative journalism on a production incident is real independence. Held at 3, not 4: open_questions[2] is an explicit alternative explanation -- whether src-0004's APT29/'Midnight Blizzard' naming error is the same phenomenon as src-0002's quantified plausible/correct split or a distinct hallucination sub-type (citation/naming fabrication vs. attribution judgment) -- and it has been articulated but never argued either way, so the counterargument is not 'explicitly addressed' as level 4 demands. src-0006 contains attribution-adjacent tasks (Threat Actor Linking, False Flag Detection) but reports accuracy/F1 deltas under mitigation, not a plausible-vs-correct split, so it is not a third source for this issue's specific claim. No open contradiction, so no g3 demotion.

task-dependent-reliability-framing.rationale: Raised from 1 (cycle 4) to 3. Scored on evidence, not on the cycle-6 candidate's self-assigned 'supported' status label -- the same discipline cycle 4 applied when it declined to let ioc-extraction's self-assigned label drive its score. On evidence, the NARROW claim (CTI reliability varies sharply by sub-task rather than being one uniform property) is now backed by three mutually independent WITHIN-study demonstrations, not just cross-benchmark synthesis: src-0006 (one consistent design across multiple CTI sub-tasks, F1/AUC ~0.20-0.90; e.g. Source Reliability Scoring AUC 0.912 vs 0.547), src-0002 (one benchmark, one model set: CTI-MCQ/CTI-RCM 71-72% vs CTI-ATE F1 0.64), and src-0001 (one study: extraction max CI width 0.02 vs generation 0.06, and markedly worse generation calibration -- all re-verified live this cycle). Different authors, benchmarks, model sets and years. That clears the level-3 bar of >=2 independent sources; the cycle-4 score of 1 was correct at the time only because no candidate with supported status existed and the synthesis was admittedly untested as a unit. Hard-capped at 3 and NOT 4, for two reasons that should be read together: (a) the claim now supported is materially narrower than this issue as titled -- the specific 'mechanical extraction < classification < attribution < generation' ordinal axis, which is the issue's distinguishing content, is not merely unverified but positively in doubt, since src-0006 found its three failure patterns cut across all four of its pipeline stages including contextualization/extraction-type tasks; scored on that axis alone this issue would still be a 1; (b) that counterargument is raised in open_questions[0] but never engaged, and open_questions[1] (does human-in-the-loop validation specifically transfer to reasoning-heavy tasks) and [2] (does the conclusion survive an independent LANCE/PRISM replication) were both searched for in cycle 6 and came back empty -- sharpened, still open. A future cycle should consider splitting this issue so the supported narrow claim and the questioned ordinal axis are scored separately, since one number is currently averaging over both. No open contradiction, so no g3 demotion.

institutional-incident-real-world-impact.rationale: Unchanged from cycle 4. Sole candidate's evidence is src-0004 only (Heise/Der Spiegel on ENISA): single-source support caps this at 2. Cycle 4's G2 retrospection re-fetched the URL and re-confirmed the 26-of-492 incorrect-footnote figure, the APT29/'Midnight Blizzard' hallucination fingerprint, and ENISA's 'human errors' response permitting AI for 'minor editorial revisions'. Re-verification of one source is not a second source. All 3 open_questions remain unaddressed, and the first of them (industry base rate across CTI publishers) is the reason this issue's own candidate explicitly claims existence but not frequency -- a scope limit that would block level 4 even if a second source arrived. No new evidence has been added for this issue since cycle 1. No open contradiction, so no g3 demotion.
